label: recorded Jev judgments, synthetic spike data

standards.title: States a fact, not a work log
Decisions say what was rejected or why
Summary is backed by the body

nodes.summary: Stripe webhook handling in harbor-api is asynchronous.
nodes.context: The handler acknowledges the event right away and puts it on the billing queue. Processing inline was rejected: Stripe retries when the endpoint is slow to answer, and invoice finalization can be slow, which produced duplicate deliveries.

nodes.summary: Migrated cart state to Zustand after discussing with the team.
nodes.context: The Zustand store lives in src/state/store.ts. The cart slice was migrated first; the other slices still use the old context providers.

nodes.summary: Terraform state lives in an S3 bucket with DynamoDB locking; Terraform Cloud was rejected because the team did not want a second place to manage access.
nodes.context: State bucket is harbor-tfstate with versioning on. State locking is not configured yet; two applies at once would both proceed.

nodes.summary: Harbor is kept as three repositories (harbor-api, harbor-web, harbor-infra) instead of a monorepo, so that infrastructure changes go through their own approval path.
nodes.context: A monorepo was tried on a branch. The blocker was that the infra approvers would have been required reviewers on every application pull request.

nodes.summary: API versioning approach was decided in the March sync.
nodes.context: See meeting notes.

nodes.summary: Feature flags are evaluated on the server side and handed to the web app.
nodes.context: Client-side evaluation was considered and rejected: it would ship the names of unreleased flags inside the bundle. harbor-api evaluates the flags and harbor-web reads them from the bootstrap payload.

nodes.summary: Set up node-pg-migrate and added the first migration.
nodes.context: Migration scripts are wired into package.json as migrate:up and migrate:down. Files live in migrations/.

nodes.summary: The CI workflow runs on a custom runner setup.
nodes.context: Jobs moved from GitHub-hosted runners to self-hosted runners in the build VPC after the hosted-minutes bill grew sharply. The runner label is harbor-build.

nodes.summary: Use date-fns for all date formatting in harbor-web.
nodes.context: Moment.js remains the date library across the app. The bundle-size ticket that proposed a switch was closed without changes.

nodes.summary: Going with Postmark for transactional email.
nodes.context: The mailer reads its credentials from the POSTMARK_TOKEN environment variable. It seemed better overall.

nodes.summary: All harbor-api JSON error responses use the envelope {error: {code, message, requestId}}.
nodes.context: toErrorResponse in src/http/errors.ts builds the envelope. Handlers throw HarborError and never write error bodies themselves.

nodes.summary: Use descriptive names.
nodes.context: Avoid abbreviations where possible.

nodes.summary: Custom React hooks in harbor-web live under src/hooks and are named use<Thing>.
nodes.context: Most hooks currently sit in src/utils/hooks. Moving them is planned but has not started; useCart is the only file under src/hooks.

nodes.summary: Test files sit next to the file they test.
nodes.context: For example Button.tsx and Button.test.tsx share a folder.

nodes.summary: Every Terraform resource that supports tags carries owner, env and cost_center tags through the shared tags local.
nodes.context: The shared tags local sets only env and managed_by. owner and cost_center were proposed in review but were not added.

nodes.summary: Always log with structured fields.
nodes.context: Logging should be consistent.

nodes.summary: Agreed in review to stop using any; cleaned up the worst offenders.
nodes.context: The ESLint config for harbor-web lives in .eslintrc.cjs. The import-order rule was also turned on.

nodes.summary: Outbound HTTP calls retry with backoff.
nodes.context: This applies to calls made from harbor-api workers to third-party APIs. The web app never retries on its own.

nodes.summary: rotateRefreshToken issues a new refresh token on every use and revokes the whole token family when an already-used token is presented.
nodes.context: Each refresh token row carries a family id. Presenting a token marked used sets revoked on every row in that family and returns 401.

nodes.summary: Fixed the bug in login where users got logged out.
nodes.context: Root cause: the session cookie was set without SameSite=Lax, so the browser dropped it on the OAuth redirect. Cookie options are now set in one place, src/auth/cookies.ts.

nodes.summary: Passwords are hashed with bcrypt in hashPassword.
nodes.context: hashPassword uses argon2id. Older bcrypt hashes are detected by prefix and upgraded to argon2id the next time the user logs in.

nodes.summary: Updated tests.
EventLedger makes webhook handling idempotent.
nodes.context: Each Stripe event id is inserted into webhook_events under a unique constraint. A conflict means the event was already handled, and the handler returns 200 without side effects.

nodes.summary: Need to ask Priya whether invoice.finalized should also trigger the dunning email; blocked until she is back on Thursday.
nodes.context: Left a comment on ticket HB-2291.

nodes.summary: Worked on the plan_id backfill migration, ran into lock timeouts, will pick it up again tomorrow.
nodes.context: Batching the update in small chunks avoided the lock timeout on the subscriptions table in staging.

nodes.summary: Rate limiting is handled.
nodes.context: There is no rate limiting in harbor-api yet. The RateLimiter class is a stub whose allow method always returns true.

nodes.summary: Refactored CheckoutForm and cleaned things up.
nodes.context: CheckoutForm is now split into AddressStep and PaymentStep. Validation moved to zod schemas in src/features/checkout/schema.ts.

nodes.summary: apiClient attaches the CSRF token from the harbor_csrf cookie to every mutating request and retries once after a 401 by calling /auth/refresh.
nodes.context: apiClient does not retry. On a 401 it clears local state and redirects to /login. The CSRF header is X-Harbor-CSRF.

nodes.summary: Fixed the flaky cart test.
nodes.context: The test awaited a fake timer that was never advanced. It now uses vi.useFakeTimers together with advanceTimersByTime.

nodes.summary: Design tokens reference.
nodes.context: The Figma library 'Harbor UI' is the source of truth. tokens.css is generated by scripts/build-tokens.mjs and must not be edited by hand.

nodes.summary: Looked into bundle size, it's mostly fine.
nodes.context: The main chunk is very large because the charting library is bundled eagerly. Lazy-loading the reports route would cut it substantially and should be done before launch.

nodes.summary: TODO for Marcus: run the axe audit on the settings pages before the release and file tickets for anything serious.
nodes.context: The release checklist assigns the axe audit of the settings pages to Marcus. Findings rated serious or worse need a ticket.

nodes.summary: The vpc module sets up the subnets and NAT routing for each environment.
nodes.context: Private and public subnets are created in every availability zone. Staging routes private egress through a single NAT gateway; production has one NAT gateway per zone.

nodes.summary: Deploys to production require a manual approval in the 'production' GitHub environment; staging deploys run automatically on merge to main.
nodes.context: In deploy.yml both the staging and the production job run automatically on merge to main. No environment protection rule exists.

nodes.summary: Tweaked CI caching, builds seem faster now.
nodes.context: The cache key now includes the lockfile hash. restore-keys fall back to the branch prefix.

nodes.summary: Remember to rotate the staging database password after the contractor's access ends; Dana said she would handle the vault side.
A request id created at the edge is forwarded as X-Request-Id from harbor-web through harbor-api and appears in every log line and error envelope, so one id traces a user action across both services.
nodes.context: The load balancer adds X-Request-Id when it is missing. The web app's apiClient copies it onto outgoing calls, and the API logger and toErrorResponse both include it.

nodes.summary: Environment names are dev, staging and production everywhere: Terraform workspaces, GitHub environments, the API's HARBOR_ENV and the web app's VITE_HARBOR_ENV.
nodes.context: Terraform workspaces are called dev, stage and prod. The application configs use development, staging and production.

nodes.summary: On-call handbook.
nodes.context: Link: wiki/on-call. Covers the paging policy for API, web and infrastructure incidents.

nodes.summary: Summary of the release work this sprint: coordinated the API deploy with the web release and updated the infra runbook.
nodes.context: Release order is infra, then API, then web, because the web build reads the API's OpenAPI spec at build time.

a.context: Each refresh token row carries a family id. Presenting a used token revokes every row in that family.

b.summary: Refresh tokens are single-use: each refresh returns a fresh token, and replaying an old one invalidates every token descended from the same login.

b.context: The class that does this is EventLedger.
